**How to read this.** `exact of reached` is the share of walks that put the mark on the body truly k from
the anchor, among walks where that body entered a field before the image ran out. `anchor held` is how
often the node the count started from really was the anchor -- a diagnostic, never a gate. Counting uses
NO learned component, so no spine is withheld on the encoder's account; where a detector supplies the
boxes, the arm is restricted to cases held out from THAT detector.

**WHAT THE ARMS SUPPORT, stated so no draft overstates it.**

1. Counting across overlapping fields is exact WHEN THE BOXES ARE RIGHT: 834/834 from C2 at three bodies
   of overlap (76 whole-spine studies), 618/618 on the 79-case true-box control, 99.66% of 6,255 reached
   walks on all 801 abdominopelvic spines, and on REAL RADIOGRAPHS 1,204/1,209 walks (99.67%) counting
   down from C2 on 262 cervical films -- the largest real-film arm, and the one to quote.
2. The risk is THE BOXES, not the anchor alone. Identifying the anchor by class raised a render
   detector from 30.1% to only 44.1% and refused 507 of 625 walks, because that detector both rarely
   names a sacrum and duplicates bodies. Refusal converts wrong answers into declines, not right ones.
   Do not write "the anchor is the whole risk".
3. The same film detector is REGION-DEPENDENT: 95/95 exact on lumbar films from the sacrum, 29.9% on
   cervical films from C2, where most failures occur within a single exposure -- bad boxes, not bad links.
4. NEEDLE CONFIRMATION works, and THE METAL IS NOT FREE. On 801 abdominopelvic spines a confirming frame
   with a radiopaque needle drawn in it was assigned to the right vertebra on 99.31% of 5,385
   confirmations (placed 99.94%, 4 ms per match) against 99.48% on the identical needle-free frames, a
   cost of 0.17 points. That corpus has NO CERVICAL SPINE. On 501 whole-spine studies the same pair reads
   98.57% against 99.15%, a cost of 0.58 points, and the whole difference is cervical: 84.58% with the
   needle against 93.09% without, 8.5 points, in the region that was already weakest. Thoracic and lumbar
   lost 0.19 and 0.37 points, an ordering that does NOT follow body size, so report the regional result
   and offer no mechanism. Do not write "the metal does not pull the correlation match" -- that was
   written from the abdominopelvic corpus alone and the only other corpus refutes it. Moving the C-arm
   before confirming costs little: 99.20% at half a body, 99.08% at a full body. 975 confirmations were
   excluded because a 9-inch field centred on the target did not contain it wholly -- a re-shoot, not an
   error.
5. Naming the same chains with the trained network reaches 94-96%, BELOW the count on the same protocol.
   That is the division-of-labour argument: counting is exact and needs no network; the network's job is
   to decide which alphabet a variant spine has, not to identify each body from morphology.
6. THE RESTRICTED SEARCH WINDOW IS NOT THE MECHANISM. This was asserted in this project before it was
   measured; the window ablation below measured it. Widening the half-width from 0.6 of a vertebral body
   to 2.1 leaves counting at 98.9-99.6%, so correlation over two bodies of overlap is decisive on its own.
   What the window buys is the last fraction: it is the only setting at which the whole-spine corpus has
   zero errors, and it cuts wrong placements on the 801-spine corpus by two thirds. On the whole-spine
   corpus the effect is NOT monotone (0, then 8, then 3 errors), and at those counts no mechanism should
   be read into the difference between the two widened settings. Do not write "restricting the search to
   the commanded step is the mechanism"; write what it is worth.
